review_scope: External drift supplement, not an artifact of the original locked tree

observations.statement: The documented CLI feature requires experimental enablement; no enablement command was executed.
Available extension definitions are discoverable by registered name; execution requires supplying the definition's actual inputs rather than copying an illustrative schema.
Resource limits are recommended, not mandatory in this source; run approval depends on permission settings and extension entry points.
Terminal runs require a definition accessible outside session-only storage; input JSON and prior tool/URL permissions are separate requirements. Unapproved requests are denied rather than prompting.
Illustrative command arguments must be adapted to the actual workflow; JSON can be inline or read from a file. No sample command or extension was executed.
Completed commands return a result when supplied; paused or stopped runs report status and run identity. Configured and default limits remain applicable.

A result file contains only the returned value, not progress or run details. It is written only after successful completion with a result; existing output survives failed, interrupted or paused runs and therefore can be stale evidence.

Automation requires configured authentication and agent permissions. Repository extension trust enablement permits code execution independently of agent tool grants, so neither switch should be inferred from a documentation example.
Machine-readable output includes workflow identity, run ID, status and returned result; silent output only suppresses progress, not permission or completion requirements.
Session-scoped authoring can require separate authoring/registration approvals. Successful creation and registration do not start or verify a run.
Persisting a session extension copies its definition, not original execution history or saved progress.
Personal and repository extension destinations have different sharing scope; repository consumers require an updated checkout and extension loading, followed by availability verification.
Plugin publication is a distinct distribution action, not implied authorization for this project's public release.
CLI run details display reported phases, active and cumulative agent counts, elapsed active time and credit usage, with separate pause and cancel operations.
App monitoring is restricted to local sessions; client controls expose pause/cancel and reported run details, not independent acceptance receipts.
If OpenTelemetry is enabled, each execution or resumption creates an invoke_workflow span linking agent activity; trace configuration and actual trace integrity remain unverified.
Only resumable paused or limit-stopped runs can reuse saved completed work; unsaved work may repeat and increased limits include previously consumed usage.
Canceled runs cannot be resumed in the documented interface; cancellation must not be represented as a recoverable pause.
CLI and app use distinct resumption controls, including explicit limit increases where needed; no such runtime operation was exercised.
Session prompt scheduling is described as a capability; a schedule example does not establish a durable scheduler, executed recurrence or authorization to create one.

remaining_dependencies: Both published version bodies and render provenance
